correctness.summary: The proof-audit result is correct. Under the source paper's own contradiction hypothesis, let A be any pseudo-amenable Banach algebra with bounded approximate identity of the fixed bound that is not approximately amenable. The same closure mechanism used by the source sends A to B=A⊕^0 c0(I) for arbitrary sets I, and choosing |I|>|A| gives |B|>|A|. The canonical projection B→A shows that if B were approximately amenable then A would be as well, so B remains a counterexample. Cardinality also makes B non-isomorphic to A and rules out the reverse absorption required by the source order, hence [A] has a strict successor. Choosing I above any prescribed cardinal makes the counterexample types unbounded in cardinality, so no set-sized skeleton can contain all of them. The source's direct-sum construction only supplies upper bounds for set-indexed chains; ordinary Zorn's lemma cannot be applied to this proper-class-sized collection. This invalidates that maximal-element step without deciding the amenability implication itself.

independent_checks: Reconstructed the strict-successor argument using the quotient projection B→A and cardinality rather than relying on the record's prose.
Checked that unbounded counterexample cardinalities preclude any set of representatives by taking the supremum of the representative cardinalities.
Checked that set-indexed chain upper bounds for a proper class do not satisfy the hypotheses of ordinary Zorn's lemma.
limitations: The audit does not prove that pseudo-amenability plus a bounded approximate identity fails to imply approximate amenability.
No counterexample to the amenability implication is constructed.
The finding concerns the unrestricted Zorn argument in arXiv:2609.17428v1; an unrelated proof or carefully specified foundational reformulation could still work.
The motivating preprint is extremely recent, so a not-yet-indexed revision or comment may duplicate the correction.

originality.summary: The set/class distinction, cardinal enlargement and the scope of ordinary Zorn's lemma are standard foundations. The source preprint is a September 2026 claim of equivalence, and targeted searches for the exact preprint together with Zorn/proper-class/cardinality/correction terminology did not locate a public correction or earlier statement of this specific obstruction. The supported contribution is therefore the application of standard foundational facts to the source's own c0(I) closure mechanism, not any new set-theoretic principle. Because the preprint is very recent, unindexed author comments or parallel proof audits remain a real priority risk.

scientific_value.summary: The obstruction strikes the central maximality step of a current functional-analysis preprint presented as closing a known proof gap. It also isolates a reusable warning for maximality arguments over Banach-algebra classes closed under arbitrarily large c0-sums. The result is valuable as a correction even though it neither supplies a counterexample nor settles the underlying implication.
